anchor.statement: Definition 9.4 (Finite correction state). For j ∈ N ∪ {0}, a state at stage j consists of real fields of the form (9.7) with the following properties. The wave w is a sum of curls of supported wave potentials with the fixed label phases, and the mean correction ( β , v, γ ) is the sum of a curl of an azimuthal potential and a direct azimuthal field. In particular, both velocity corrections are exactly divergence-free. The source supports, finite harmonic sets, smooth zero extensions, and physical residual decomposition are as in Proposition 9.3. The normalized nonzero harmonics G [ j] wave of G [ j] ∗ , the exact tangential mean residuals, and the three integral defects obey G [j] wave ∈ W B j , E θ , E z ∈ M C ∗ j , (P, J θ , J z ) ∈ S C ∗ j , B j = 1 2 + σ j , C ∗ j = 1 + σ j , σ j = 1 5 + j 10 , (9.8) with the following bounds for the total velocity and pressure corrections w ∈ W 1/2 , w − w tan 0 ∈ W 0.68 , v, γ , p m ∈ M 0.9 , β ∈ M 1.9 . (9.9) Wave assertions refer to each grouped nonzero harmonic per label. The two normalized angular-momentum and axial-flux moments are maintained exactly: ∫︂ ∞ 0 R 2 ⟨v⟩ Y dR = 0, ∫︂ ∞ 0 R⟨ γ ⟩ Y dR = 0. (9.10) The pressure reconstruction is part of the state. Consequently, the radial residual of every such state is − ρ P plus the flat cutoff remainder of Proposition 8.3.
anchor.title: Finite correction state

correspondence.by: Christian Garry (drafted with Claude Code; second review by ChatGPT, checked)
correspondence.note: Carries (9.8)–(9.10) with a real σ in place of the stage j (σ_j = 1/5 + j/10), defects in an unweighted slow class for S, and additional fields (wave pressure in W^1, covariance in M^1, smoothness, periodicity, support and representation data), so it defines a narrower notion than Definition 9.4.
